notes: cics-crucible condition-handling / hc-readq-td (Apache-2.0 corpus, owner OK 2026-10-31 for the ladder, #6072): READQ TD: destructive FIFO read of an intrapartition queue (oldest first, the read destroys the record), QZERO on an empty or drained queue, QIDERR on an undefined queue (READQ / WRITEQ / DELETEQ), DELETEQ TD then READQ, LENGERR on a short INTO area. Scenarios restate the crucible's terminal steps; the oracle is GnuCOBOL plus the stub, not the crucible's hand-written logs.

scenarios.name: fifo
scenarios.why: WRITEQ TD of items of 5, 7 and 8 bytes, then READQ TD x4 into an 8-byte area: oldest first, each read destroys its record (5, 7, 8 bytes), the fourth is QZERO; the queue ends empty

scenarios.name: seeded
scenarios.why: HCQ1 starts with one item; WRITEQ TD appends a second; READQ TD returns the seeded item first, then the written one, then QZERO

scenarios.name: empty
scenarios.why: READQ TD of an empty queue: QZERO, the INTO area is not written

scenarios.name: undefined
scenarios.why: READQ TD, WRITEQ TD and DELETEQ TD of HCNQ, a queue the CSD does not define: QIDERR each

scenarios.name: deleteq
scenarios.why: WRITEQ TD of three items, DELETEQ TD of the queue, then READQ TD: the data is gone, QZERO

scenarios.name: lengerr
scenarios.why: an 8-byte item read into a 4-byte area with LENGTH(4): LENGERR, the first 4 bytes are moved and LENGTH comes back 8

scenarios.name: unmatched-mode
scenarios.why: takes the EVALUATE/IF arm no crucible scenario reaches: a mode no WHEN names (falls through)
